entries.summary: At 13:37 EST, the latest verified 13:15 assessment remains bearish. Fresh source review found no sufficiently timestamped, synchronized later QQQ/SOX/VXN/VIX/breadth tape to establish a new regime change. A November 16 trading diary reported QQQ transactions near $664.49 at 11:14 and $670.27 in its 11:38 update, suggesting an intraday rebound in traded prices, but these are discretionary execution reports rather than exchange-certified contemporaneous quotes and cannot confirm sustained recovery. No new Open Watch event was recorded. Downside risk remains elevated ahead of Tuesday's macro releases and Nvidia earnings and Wednesday's FOMC minutes.
bullish: A recovery in breadth and VIX alongside semiconductor leadership could still create a sharp relief rally.
Nvidia's pending results could reverse AI-sector sentiment; no earnings outcome is known.
bearish: Nasdaq 100 fell more than 2% in early cash trading versus S&P 500 approximately -0.7%, according to FT.
VIX spot jumped 11.6% to 21.53 and Nasdaq decliners outnumbered advancers 2.3:1 in a separate MarketWatch intraday report.
Elevated reported Treasury yields near 5.13% 10Y and 4.85% 2Y add valuation pressure; paired timing unverified.

editorial.marketOverview: Nasdaq remains in a technology-led risk-off environment according to the latest confirmed intraday evidence: the noon Nasdaq Composite decline of 1.72% and separate FT Nasdaq-100 decline exceeding 2%. Those observations are not synchronized with the earlier MarketWatch VIX and breadth readings. Newer precise index/sector prints were not independently verified at this checkpoint.
editorial.whatChanged: No material new verified market catalyst or regime change was established since the 13:15 ET assessment. A November 16 trading diary disclosed QQQ purchase/execution prices near $664.49 and $670.27 at late-morning timestamps, consistent with intraday volatility but not sufficient to establish a lasting recovery. The curated Open Watch event file still shows 164 records, last updated 15:22:27 UTC.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Semiconductor relative weakness and negative Nasdaq breadth remain the dominant confirmed evidence. An intraday bounce in QQQ transactions cannot invalidate bearish positioning without sustained recovery in QQQ, SOX and breadth alongside easing VIX. The indicative 10Y–2Y spread is +28 basis points from rounded secondary yields (5.13% minus 4.85% multiplied by 100); the pair is not an official synchronized observation. FedWatch direct odds, VXN, and fresh oil prices remain unavailable.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 16: bearish until confirmed closing QQQ/SOX recovery and breadth improvement; an intraday rebound is possible but unconfirmed. Tuesday November 17: retail sales and industrial production can shift growth/rates pricing, with Nvidia results expected after the close subject to issuer confirmation. Wednesday November 18: housing starts and FOMC minutes are rate-sensitive risk checkpoints. Downside continuation is favored over a sustained rally absent confirmation.
editorial.bullCase: A genuine reversal would require QQQ and SOX to stabilize and outperform, declining issues to retreat toward parity, and VIX to ease; positive Nvidia guidance could catalyze a rebound, but its result is not yet known.
editorial.bearCase: Further chip weakness, elevated VIX and poor breadth into Monday's close would favor continuation; disappointing macro or Nvidia guidance or hawkish FOMC minutes could amplify pressure, but none of those outcomes has occurred.
editorial.watchNext: Verify closing QQQ/Nasdaq and SOX, spot VXN/VIX, breadth, 10Y and 2Y yields from official contemporaneous sources, Brent and WTI and directly sourced CME FedWatch. Recheck Open Watch event IDs for newly curated catalysts and monitor Tuesday's scheduled macro and Nvidia releases.
